current_example.title: Example: Calculating a Determinant After Multiplying a Row by a Number

q-130682.name: Question 1
q-130682.problem: Suppose $X$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(X)=55.$ The matrix $Y$ is obtained from $X$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{5}↔{R}_{3}$ (switching the fifth and the third rows). What is the value of $det(Y)?$
q-130682.worked_solution:
Since swapping any two rows changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite sign, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =-det(X) \\  & =-(55) \\  & =-55.\end{aligned}
$$

q-43077.name: Question 6
q-43077.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $6\times 6$ matrix and $det(A)=35.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:=-\frac{3}{5}{R}_{1}.$ What is the value of $det(B)?$
q-43077.worked_solution:
The row operation applied to $A$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $-\frac{3}{5}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =-\frac{3}{5}det(A) \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}\cdot 35 \\  & =-21.\end{aligned}
$$

q-42502.name: Question 7
q-42502.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(A)=2.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}:=\frac{3}{2}{R}_{3}.$ What is the value of $det(B)?$
q-42502.worked_solution:
The row operation applied to $A$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $\frac{3}{2}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =\frac{3}{2}det(A) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}

q-42502.html:
Question 7
?

Suppose A is a 5×5 matrix and det(A)=2. The matrix B is obtained from A by applying the elementary row operation R3:=32R3. What is the value of det(B)?

a
6
b
32
c
3
d
−3
e
2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The row operation applied to A consists of multiplying a row by the number 32.

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

det(B)=32det(A)=32⋅2=3.
